app.title: Omniphony Studio
app.subtitle: Spatial Control
log.title: Logs
log.noMatch: No logs match the current filter.
log.copySuccess: {count} log entries copied to the clipboard.
log.orenderAutostartLaunched: No local renderer answering — standby renderer auto-started.
log.orenderAutostartFailed: Local renderer auto-start failed repeatedly — check the orender log and settings.
osc.label: OSC
osc.infoBody:
Host: target host used for OSC communication.

Omniphony Port: port where `orender` sends state and receives control.

Listen Port: local port used by the visualizer to receive OSC. `0` lets the system choose one automatically.
help.updates.check: Check GitHub for a newer Omniphony release each time Studio starts and show a banner when one is available. Nothing is downloaded automatically.
help.osc.host: Target host for OSC communication with the renderer.
help.osc.omniphonyPort: UDP port where orender (the renderer) receives control and sends state.
help.osc.listenPort: Local UDP port Studio listens on for OSC state. 0 lets the system choose one.
help.osc.autoStartRenderer: When nothing answers on a local (127.x) target, Studio launches a standby renderer automatically. It yields the OSC port to an mpv-embedded renderer during playback and comes back when mpv exits.
help.osc.mpvOrender: mpv only uses the engine when asked to (ad=orender). This writes that line into your mpv.conf, in a marked block placed before any profile section so it applies globally. Turning it off comments the line out; nothing else in the file is touched.
help.osc.keepRendererAlive: Leave the Studio-launched renderer running after closing Studio. Off (default): it quits with Studio.
help.osc.metering: Stream per-object and per-speaker level meters over OSC to drive the meters in the UI. The rate (Hz) sets how often levels are published — higher is smoother but more traffic.
help.display.language: UI language. “Auto” follows your system locale; otherwise the chosen language is used for all Studio text.
help.display.mpvOverlay: Show the spatial overlay (objects, speakers, trails, heatmaps) on top of the video when playing through mpv-omniphony. Purely visual — it doesn't affect the audio.
help.display.grid: Draw the reference grid / room box in the 3D scene to gauge positions and scale. Display only.
help.display.showObjects: Show the audio objects (sources) as markers in the 3D scene. Off only hides them; rendering is unaffected.
help.display.objectColors: Tint each object with its own colour (from the stream/metadata when available) instead of a single uniform colour.
help.display.objectLabels: Show each object's name/label next to its marker in the scene.
help.display.showObjectDetails: Show per-object details (position, level, size…) in the Objects list.
help.display.objectDisplayMode: How objects are drawn in the 3D scene: a flat circle, a transparent sphere, or a diffuse sphere. Display only.
help.display.objectSphereSize: Radius of the object markers in the 3D scene. Display only.
help.display.speakerLabels: Show each speaker's name next to its marker in the scene.
help.display.speakerBands: Show a small frequency-extent gauge beside each speaker on a log axis (20 Hz at the bottom, 20 kHz at the top). The lit segment is the speaker's crossover pass-band, so you can tell its role at a glance: a low-pass (sub) fills the bottom, a high-pass (tweeter) the top, a band-pass (mid) a floating middle segment, and a full-band speaker the whole bar. Each band present in the layout's crossover split gets its own solid colour, ordered low→high, so speakers in different bands stand out. Display only.
help.display.speakerFaceListener: Rotate each speaker so its front (marked by a small driver disc) points at the listener at the centre of the room. Off, the speakers are drawn as plain cubes. Display only — it does not change the audio.
help.display.speakerSize: Radius of the speaker markers in the 3D scene. Display only.
help.trail.mode: How object motion trails are drawn: a diffuse fading cloud or a connected line.
help.trail.duration: How long a trail stays visible, in seconds.
help.trail.teleport: Jump distance above which a move is treated as a teleport, breaking the trail instead of connecting it.
help.heatmap.speakerVolume: Overlay a per-speaker volume heatmap on the scene, colouring each speaker by how much signal it currently carries.
help.heatmap.crossoverBand: Which crossover band every heatmap shows — the per-speaker volume, the energy deviation and the discontinuity field all follow this one selection, as do the effective-render and dominant-speaker readouts. "All bands" switches each heatmap to its own all-bands composite.
help.heatmap.objectEnergy: Overlay the objects' energy field: a volumetric heatmap of where object energy is concentrated in the room.
help.heatmap.smooth: Smooth the heatmap gradient between cells instead of showing hard cell boundaries.
help.heatmap.colormap: Colour gradient mapping energy to colour. “Custom” opens a gradient editor.
help.heatmap.radius: Falloff radius of each object's energy splat in the field. Display only.
help.heatmap.mix: Blends the field between time-accumulated energy and instantaneous peak.
help.heatmap.gammaAccumulate: Gamma applied to the accumulated-energy component; higher compresses low values.
help.heatmap.gammaMip: Gamma applied to the peak component; higher compresses low values.
help.binaural.hrtf: Head-Related Transfer Function used to spatialize over headphones. KEMAR (measured) is a real measured dummy-head set; Synthetic is a lightweight analytic model; SOFA file loads your own .sofa (a personal HRTF externalizes far better than a generic one — see sofacoustics.org).
help.binaural.headRadius: Radius of the listener's head in centimetres. Sets the interaural time/level differences; match your own head for sharper localization (average ≈ 8.75 cm).
help.binaural.pinnaPreset: Per-listener D_n preset from Brown & Duda (1998), Table I — the only parameter the model individualizes. PB & NH and RD are the published subject fits; pick whichever localizes elevation best for you.
help.binaural.pinnaDScale: Fine scale on the elevation factor D_n: how strongly the pinna notches move with elevation. 100% is the chosen preset as published; raise/lower to sharpen or soften the vertical effect.
help.binaural.pinnaDepth: Strength of the parametric pinna echoes. 0% is the bare head-shadow model (≈ Synthetic, no elevation cue); 100% is full pinna colouration that adds the elevation and front/back cues.
help.binaural.prtfDepth: Amount of PRTF colouration for the Spagnol structural model (dry/wet between the bare head shadow and the full resonances + notches). 0% ≈ Synthetic; 100% is the full pinna model. The concha resonances are what reduce the in-head impression.
help.binaural.prtfFreqScale: Scales every resonance and notch centre frequency of the PRTF model (notch freq ∝ 1/pinna distance). Below 100% lowers them (larger pinna), above raises them — a one-knob stand-in for photo-based individualization. Tune until elevation feels right.
help.binaural.distanceScale: Metres represented by one scene unit. Scales how far objects sound from the listener — larger values push sources further away.
help.binaural.airAbsorption: Roll off high frequencies with distance, as air does in reality. Adds a sense of depth; disable for a drier, closer sound.
help.binaural.earlyReflections: Render the first wall/floor/ceiling reflections of the virtual listening room. They strongly improve externalization (sound outside the head) at a modest cost.
help.binaural.reflectionLevel: Loudness of the early reflections relative to the direct sound. Higher feels more roomy; too high smears localization.
help.binaural.room: Dimensions (width × depth × height, in metres) of the virtual listening room that produces the reflections and reverb. Bigger rooms give longer, sparser reflections.
help.binaural.lateReverb: Render the diffuse reverberant tail of the virtual room (after the early reflections). Adds envelopment; disable for a dead, anechoic sound.
help.binaural.reverbLevel: Loudness of the late-reverb tail relative to the direct sound.
help.binaural.rt60: Reverberation time of the virtual room — seconds for the tail to decay by 60 dB. Longer sounds like a larger/more reflective space.
help.binaural.headTracking: Rotate the binaural scene with your head so sources stay fixed in the room. Feed orientation over OSC from the Android app Sensors2OSC (official repo: https://github.com/SensorApps/Sensors2OSC ; also on F-Droid as org.sensors2.osc). Enable its Game Rotation Vector sensor and point it at this machine's OSC port.
help.binaural.oscAddress: OSC address carrying the head-orientation data (e.g. /gamerotationvector from Sensors2OSC). Leave empty to disable head tracking.
help.binaural.trackFormat: How the incoming orientation is encoded: Auto detects it, or force Quaternion, Rotation vector, or Euler angles to match your sender.
help.binaural.trackSmoothing: Low-pass smoothing of the head pose. Higher is steadier but laggier; lower is snappier but jitterier.
help.binaural.invertRotation: Flip the tracking direction if the scene turns the wrong way relative to your head.
help.heatmap.resolution: Grid resolution of the energy field. Higher is smoother but costlier to render.
help.heatmap.refresh: How often the energy field's 3D texture is rebuilt and re-uploaded to the GPU. Lower is more fluid but uses more GPU upload bandwidth (which raises memory use on Windows); higher is lighter. The volume still renders every frame either way.
help.heatmap.opacity: Overall opacity of the energy-field overlay.
help.drc.mode: Dynamic-range-compression profile applied to the decoded stream (from the bitstream's DRC metadata).
help.drc.weight: How strongly the selected DRC profile is applied, from 0% (off) to 100% (full).
help.drc.loudness: Enable loudness / dialog-normalization handling from the stream's metadata.
osc.mpvOrenderConflict: Line {line} already sets a decoder: {text}. Remove it to use this switch.
about.title: About
about.descriptionFallback: Omniphony is an open spatial-audio project built around realtime rendering, transport, control, and monitoring tools for object-based audio workflows. Omniphony Studio is the visual control surface of that ecosystem.
room.title: Room Geometry
room.infoBody:
Room geometry defines the physical room dimensions, in meters, used to map normalized scene coordinates to meters.

Width is the reference and pins the scale; Front, Rear, Height and Lower are entered directly in meters. The Y center blend only appears when Front and Rear differ.

These values affect distance-based processing and the spatial interpretation of the 3D scene.
help.twoDSources: How fixed-channel sources are rendered — for example stereo, 5.1, 7.1 or a fixed 7.1.4 presentation. Each channel can independently be placed and panned over the output layout (Virtual), or routed only to its matching speaker (Direct); LFE is direct by default. Synthetic objects are a separate optional stage. Dynamic object audio is never converted by these controls, and every setting remains editable without an active stream.
help.room.width: Room width in metres along X. This axis is the reference that pins the overall scale (metres per scene unit); the other dimensions are read relative to it.
help.room.front: Distance from the listener to the front wall, in metres (the +Y depth).
help.room.rear: Distance from the listener to the rear wall, in metres (the −Y depth). When it differs from Front, the Y center blend control appears.
help.room.height: Distance from the listener up to the ceiling, in metres (the +Z extent).
help.room.lower: Distance from the listener down to the floor, in metres (the −Z extent).
help.room.centerBlend: When Front and Rear depths differ, the front/back axis is warped so its front edge maps to the Front extent and its rear edge to the Rear extent. This sets the depth scale right at the listener — the slope of that warp through the centre — as a Front/Rear blend: 100/0 uses the Front scale, 0/100 the Rear scale, 50/50 the average. It shapes how the front-to-rear scale change is spread around you; it does not move the listener, which always stays at the centre. Tip: turn on the Grid (under Display) to see the warp as you adjust this. Double-click to reset.
input.infoBody:
This section defines where incoming audio comes from and how Studio describes that source to the renderer.

Mode chooses between a bridged file/process input and a live device/backend path. The remaining fields define the bridge binary, imported layout, channel format, mapping, and channel handling that the renderer should expect.
help.input.mode: Where incoming audio comes from: a bridged file/process (Pipe bridge), a live PipeWire device, or a PipeWire bridge.
help.input.bridge: Path to the decoder bridge binary that feeds the renderer; leave empty to auto-detect.
help.input.pipe: Named pipe the bridge writes decoded PCM into; auto-detected when left empty.
help.input.backend: Live capture backend for device input: PipeWire (Linux) or ASIO (Windows).
help.input.node: PipeWire node name Studio creates / expects for the live input.
help.input.description: Human-readable description advertised for the live input node.
help.input.layout: Imported speaker layout describing the channel order of the live source.
help.input.channels: Number of channels in the input stream.
help.input.sampleRate: Sample rate of the input stream, in Hz.
help.input.format: Sample format of the input PCM: 32-bit float (f32) or 16-bit integer (s16).
help.input.map: Channel-mapping preset describing how input channels map to beds / objects.
input.clockInfoBody:
Clock selects which side is treated as the timing reference for the live input path.

DAC follows the output device clock. PipeWire follows the PipeWire graph clock. Upstream (advanced) trusts the capture source or bridge clock — the sink runs without a driver flag and requires an external PipeWire driver in the chain (e.g. JACK or a monitoring client). Without one, playback stalls. Prefer DAC unless you know you need this.

This choice matters when diagnosing drift, latency correction, or which side should adapt to the other.
input.lfeInfoBody:
LFE controls what happens to the input stream's low-frequency effects channel.

Object turns it into a spatial object. Direct keeps it as a dedicated direct-fed LFE path. Drop ignores it entirely.

Choose this according to how the source material was authored and how your output layout expects bass content to be routed.
audio.channelMapping.warning: These speakers can't be placed by name:
help.audio.channelMapping: How rendered output channels map to your device ports. By index (default): output port N carries layout speaker N, in order — for a custom rig wired to your layout. By name: each channel is tagged with its speaker position so a position-aware sink/AVR routes it. In by-name mode, speakers with non-standard names can't be placed and are listed as a warning.
rampMode.infoBody:
Ramping smooths abrupt position or gain changes so object motion and level updates stay more natural and produce fewer clicks or spatial jumps.

Off: disable interpolation and jump immediately to the new target.

Per frame: apply one interpolation step per decoded audio frame. This is lighter and more stepped.

Per sample (interpolated): evaluate the spatial gains once per frame and linearly interpolate them across each sample. Nearly as smooth as Per sample at roughly the cost of Per frame — the recommended smooth mode.

Per sample: re-evaluate the full spatial panning for every rendered sample. The most accurate but the most expensive.
twoDSources.syntheticConfigured: Configured synthesis; current activity is shown below
twoDSources.fixedOnly: Fixed channels only — no synthetic objects
twoDSources.status.masterOff: Configured, inactive: synthetic objects are disabled
twoDSources.status.objectStream: Configured, inactive: the stream already carries objects
twoDSources.status.inputHasHeight: Configured, inactive: the stream already carries height channels
twoDSources.status.outputHasNoHeight: Configured, inactive: the output layout has no height speaker
twoDSources.status.insufficientChannels: Configured, inactive: the source has too few compatible channels
twoDSources.stream.fixed: Current source: fixed channels rendered by Omniphony
twoDSources.stream.objects: Current source: object stream; fixed-channel synthesis is not applied
twoDSources.stream.idle: No active stream — settings remain editable
help.syntheticObjects: Master switch for every object synthesized by the renderer. Off guarantees fixed-channel rendering only, while preserving the phantom and height-generator selections for later use.
help.phantomExtract: Before the height lift, extracts the correlated content shared by channel pairs as discrete objects at their real panned position, and removes it from the source channels. The remaining decorrelated bed still feeds the height stage. Extraction: how much is pulled out. Passes: how many pairings (a ring of neighbours, then wider pairs). Lift: raises the extracted objects toward the ceiling. Per-band extraction: analyses each frequency band separately (direction and directness per band), so simultaneous sources at different positions are separated into eight sector objects; adds about 21 ms of latency to the bed while active. Passes and the relocalize switches apply to the pairwise method only. The remaining diffuse bed pairs well with the DirAC height generator. Extract heights (spectral only): when the input already carries height channels, they join the same analysis in 3D — four ceiling sector objects are added and content panned between the floor and height layers is extracted at its true intermediate elevation. Height split (spectral only): the elevation, in degrees, that reads as fully high — lower values push extracted content toward the ceiling.
help.objectGenerator: Synthesizes height objects from flat (2D) channel content — stereo, 5.1, 7.1 — so a layout with top speakers is used even when the source has no height. Off: nothing is added. Direct copy: the front/surround pairs are copied straight up. Ambience (PAD): only the diffuse, decorrelated part of each pair rises, so dialogue and centred sounds stay grounded. Object-based (3D) audio is never affected. The synthesized objects appear in the 3D view and the Objects list.
channelEdit.title: Channel Editor
channelEdit.destinationPosition: The coordinates below are the speaker's actual position.
help.channelEdit.gain: Output gain for this fixed source channel, in dB. Trims one channel relative to the others (for example to pull the LFE down); 0 dB leaves it unchanged.
layout.label: Layout:
layout.prompt.name: Layout name
edit.label: Edit:
config.presetsHint: Import a bundled speaker-layout preset (opens the presets folder)
evaluation.title: Evaluation
evaluation.infoBody:
Evaluation mode controls how speaker gains are computed for each object position.

Realtime computes directly at runtime. Precomputed polar and precomputed cartesian trade memory for faster lookups and more stable cost. Auto lets the renderer choose the best available path for the current backend and tables.
help.eval.objectSizeIntervals: Number of object-size steps baked into the precomputed tables. 0 keeps a single table (object size is then honoured only in realtime); N builds N+1 tables at sizes 0…1 and interpolates at read time, at N+1× the memory. Only affects backends that consume object size (VBAP).
help.eval.cartesianGrid: Resolution of the precomputed Cartesian gain table along X, Y, Z+ and Z− (cells per axis). Higher values give smoother panning but larger tables and longer builds.
help.eval.polarGrid: Resolution of the precomputed polar gain table: azimuth, elevation and distance step counts, plus the maximum distance. Higher values give smoother panning at the cost of larger tables.
help.distanceDiffuse.metric: Metric used to reduce an object's position to the scalar distance that drives the diffuse blend: spherical (Euclidean) or Chebyshev (cube).
help.distanceDiffuse.threshold: Normalised distance at which diffusion begins. Objects nearer than this stay localised; farther objects spread more widely.
help.distanceDiffuse.curve: Exponent shaping how sharply diffusion ramps in beyond the threshold. 1 is linear; higher is more abrupt.
help.distanceDiffuse.mirrorAxes: Axes negated to build the mirror image each object is blended with. The flips combine into a single mirror, so their number names the symmetry: one is a plane reflection, two a half-turn about the axis left alone, three an inversion through the origin. X+Y is the classic behaviour; turn them all off to disable the mirror.
help.distanceModel.metric: Metric used to reduce an object's position to the scalar distance fed to the attenuation model: spherical (Euclidean) or Chebyshev (cube).
help.hybrid.external: Backend mixed in at the cube surface (blend ratio = 1, the far end of the curve).
help.hybrid.internal: Backend mixed in at the cube centre (blend ratio = 0, the near end of the curve).
help.hybrid.metric: Metric mapping an object's position to the normalised distance that indexes the blend curve: Chebyshev reaches 1 on the cube surface, spherical at a corner.
help.hybrid.smoothing: Smooths the blend curve between control points: 0 is piecewise-linear, 1 is a full spline through the points.
backend.title: Backend
backend.file.editor.title: Edit backend file
backend.infoBody: The backend is the spatial model that turns each object's position into per-speaker gains. Pick one here; its tunable parameters, if any, appear below. The list is whatever the connected renderer registered, so it can include contributor backends too. “Restore backend” reverts a temporary runtime override back to the saved configuration.
help.backend.vbap: Vector Base Amplitude Panning — the speaker-based panner: spreads each object across the 2–3 nearest speakers on the speaker hull. The general-purpose default.
help.backend.barycenter: Barycentric weighting — a softer, more blended localisation that spreads energy across more speakers. The “Localize” parameter tightens or loosens the focus.
help.backend.experimental_distance: Experimental distance-driven solver with extra tuning controls. Less battle-tested than VBAP; useful for exploring distance-based behaviours.
help.backend.hybrid: Blends two other backends per object along a ratio curve: the External backend at ratio 1, the Internal backend at ratio 0, interpolating between them. Choose the two inner backends and the blend curve below.
help.backend.example: A minimal demonstration backend showing how to plug a custom model into the registry. Not meant for real listening.
help.backend.script: User-scriptable backend: runs a Lua script that computes the per-speaker gains. Point it at your .lua file; any parameters it declares show up below.
distance.infoBody:
Distance Diffuse blends each object with a mirrored version of itself (opposite horizontal direction) depending on distance. Close objects become wider/more diffuse, while far objects stay mostly direct.

Threshold: distance where the blend reaches 100% direct.
Curve: transition shape (faster or slower near-field blend).
spread.distanceInfoBody:
Spread from Distance derives spread from listener distance instead of relying only on object_size.

The distance curve is mapped into the global spread min/max range, so close objects can stay broad while far objects collapse toward the configured minimum.

Range sets where the distance contribution reaches zero. Curve shapes how quickly that collapse happens. Size→Spread mode still controls how object size is converted when size-based spread is in use or compared against the distance result.
trail.title: Trails
trail.infoBody:
Trails show each object's recent movement history in the 3D view.

Mode: choose between a classic line or a diffuse particle trail.
Duration: how long trail points stay visible before fading out.
effectiveRender.title: Effective render
effectiveRender.infoBody:
Shows an estimated rendered position inferred from the speakers that are currently carrying the object.

The marker is meant as a visual sanity check: it helps reveal when the rendered energy center drifts away from the nominal object position.

The thin line connects the nominal object position to that estimated effective render point.
heatmap.infoBody:
Heatmaps visualize how the renderer distributes energy across the listening area or volume.

Heatmap slices shows sectional planes, Heatmap volume shows volumetric sampling, and Heatmap band selects which frequency band is displayed.

Heatmap values controls sampling density, and Max sphere size caps the display size of each sample point. Some views are only meaningful when the current evaluation mode has the required precomputed data.

Objects energy field shows the theoretical acoustic energy radiated by the objects themselves (inverse-square from each object's current level), accumulated into stacks of slices that can be cut along any of the three axes (Width, Depth, Height). Planes per axis, Field resolution, Falloff radius and Field opacity tune the display.
help.heatmap.globalEnergy: Total energy of every speaker combined, per grid cell, shown as its deviation from unit energy. Transparent where energy is conserved, red where the render is louder, blue where it is quieter. Reveals hot seams between speaker triplets and holes left by directions the layout cannot cover. Takes over the gain-table transfer while on, so the per-speaker heatmap pauses.
help.heatmap.globalEnergyScale: Deviation that saturates the colour, in dB either way. Lower to inspect small ripples, raise to keep large holes on scale.
help.heatmap.discontinuity: Breaks in speaker usage: per grid cell, the worst jump towards a neighbouring cell. Smooth panning and triplet-edge crossings stay transparent; a hard switch between speaker configurations shows as a thin bright sheet. Level changes are ignored — the energy deviation heatmap shows those.
help.heatmap.discontinuityMode: Speaker configuration compares WHICH speakers play (normalised gain vectors, √2 = disjoint sets). Energy centroid measures how far the sound image physically jumps across the room, in room units.
help.heatmap.discontinuityScale: Jump value that saturates the colour. Lower to reveal subtle seams, raise to keep only the hard breaks visible.
vbap.title: VBAP
help.vbap.positionInterpolation: On: interpolate between neighbouring VBAP table cells for smoother spatial motion and lookup continuity. Off: nearest-cell lookup — cheaper and more deterministic, but movement can become more stepped.
drc.infoBody:
This section combines codec-side dynamic range control with renderer-side loudness correction.

DRC selects the metadata-driven compression profile, and DRC weight blends how strongly that profile is applied.

Loudness / Dialog Norm applies a gain correction derived from the source metadata so playback lands closer to the configured target level.
adaptive.title: Adaptive Resampling
help.audio.outputDevice: Audio output device the renderer plays to. “Default” follows the system's current output.
help.audio.outputBackend: Where rendered audio goes: a realtime device (PipeWire/ASIO) or a file / named pipe / stdout for capture or network streaming. Switching applies live.
help.audio.outputFile: Destination for the file backend: “-” for stdout, or a path to a regular file or a named pipe (FIFO).
help.audio.outputFileFormat: Encoding for the file backend: raw interleaved 32-bit float (consumable by ffmpeg -f f32le), or a streaming CAF container.
help.audio.namedPipe: Off: write to stdout (the pipe to the launching process). On: write to the named pipe (FIFO) or file path entered below.
help.audio.sampleRate: Output sample rate in Hz. 0 follows the device's current rate.
help.audio.targetLatency: Target end-to-end buffer latency, in ms. The adaptive controller steers the ring level toward this value.
help.adaptive.title: Enable the local PI controller that continuously nudges the resample ratio to hold the target latency. The phase and global-action controls below apply whenever drift is large, even when this is off.
help.adaptive.hardRecoverHigh: When latency drifts too high (past the high-recover entry margin), aggressively drop buffered audio to return toward target faster. Applies even when adaptive resampling is off.
help.adaptive.threshold: Drift above target, in ms, at which high-side far-mode recovery becomes eligible.
help.adaptive.hardRecoverLow: When latency falls below target by the low-recover entry margin, briefly mute and rebuild buffer latency, then stabilize before fading back in.
help.adaptive.lowRecoverEntryMargin: Drift below target, in ms, at which low-side far-mode recovery engages.
help.adaptive.lowRecoverExitMargin: Drift below target, in ms, at which low-side recovery is considered cleared.
help.adaptive.silenceFar: Mute the output while far-mode recovery is active.
help.adaptive.fadeNearReturn: Fade-in length, in ms, applied when far-mode muting ends and playback becomes audible again.
help.adaptive.updateInterval: How often the PI controller updates, in audio callbacks.
help.adaptive.max: Maximum correction clamp applied to the local resample ratio, in ppm.
help.adaptive.kpNear: Proportional gain of the PI controller. Higher reacts faster to instantaneous buffer error.
help.adaptive.ki: Integral gain of the PI controller. Corrects long-term bias and clock mismatch.
help.adaptive.integralDischarge: Fraction of the stored integral retained when the error changes sign. Has little practical effect on the current controller and is not a recommended tuning knob.
help.adaptive.lowRecoverSettleStable: How long the level must stay within the settling margin, in ms, before low-recovery is declared stable.
help.adaptive.lowRecoverSettleMargin: Band around target, in ms, within which the level must hold during the settling phase.
help.adaptive.lowRecoverRefillDeltaAlpha: EMA smoothing factor (0–1) for the refill-rate estimate used during low recovery.
help.adaptive.controlSmoothingCutoffHz: Cutoff frequency of the IIR filter smoothing the controller's ratio output, in Hz.
help.adaptive.controlSmoothingOrder: Order of the control-smoothing IIR filter: 1 (single pole) or 2 (Butterworth).
help.adaptive.usePreBridgeClock: Feed the PI servo with the pre-decoder source clock instead of the post-decode ring level, so it tracks genuine hardware drift without the decoder's batching ripple.
help.adaptive.useOutputPacing: Drain rendered PCM into the ring in lockstep with source-chunk arrival, smoothing the flow. Adds ~64 ms of startup pre-roll; removes the source-side sawtooth.
help.adaptive.disableBackpressure: Diagnostic: stop blocking the renderer when the output buffer is full — push what fits and drop the overflow. Leave off for normal playback.
adaptive.hardRecoverHigh: Hard recover high in far mode
adaptive.hardRecoverLow: Hard recover low in far mode
adaptive.usePreBridgeClockTitle: Feed the PI servo with the IEC958 source-clock signal (pre-decoder) instead of the post-decode ring level. The source clock is smooth by construction, so the PI reacts directly to genuine hardware drift without the decoder's batching ripple.
adaptive.useOutputPacingTitle: Buffer rendered speaker PCM and drain it into the ring buffer in lockstep with IEC958 chunk arrival, so the ring sees a smooth flow regardless of the decoder's burst pattern. Adds ~64 ms of pre-roll latency on startup; eliminates the 3.1 Hz sawtooth at the source.
adaptive.disableBackpressureTitle: Diagnostic: stop blocking the renderer when the output buffer is full — push what fits and drop the overflow instead of waiting. Unhooks the source (mpv) from the DAC drain clock, removing the back-pressure relaxation sawtooth at the cost of dropped samples on overflow. Leave off for normal playback.
adaptive.infoBody:
This panel now mixes two kinds of controls.

Global far actions apply whenever latency drift exceeds the High-recover entry margin, even if adaptive resampling is off.
High-recover entry margin: error above target, in milliseconds of buffer drift, at which high-side far-mode actions become eligible.
Hard recover high in far mode: aggressively drops buffered audio to return toward the target faster when latency is too high (eligible past the high-recover entry margin).
Hard recover low in far mode: temporarily mutes output and rebuilds buffer latency when it falls below target by the low-recover entry margin, then stabilizes before fade-in.
Silence in Far Mode: mutes output while far-mode recovery is active.
Fade-In on Near Return: fade applied when far-mode muting ends and playback becomes audible again.

Local resampling controller only applies when Adaptive resampling is enabled.
Update interval: how often the PI controller updates, in audio callbacks.
Adaptive Max: maximum correction clamp applied to the local resampling ratio.
Adaptive KP: proportional gain. Higher values react faster to instantaneous buffer error.
Adaptive Ki: integral gain. It corrects long-term bias and clock mismatch.
Integral discharge: fraction of stored integral retained when the error changes sign. Lower values dump old controller energy more aggressively.

Pause freezes the resampling controller, and Reset ratio is available while paused to return the ratio to neutral.
telemetry.infoBody:
raw is the instantaneous measured latency; its markers show the recent low/high window.

ctrl is the smoothed control latency used by the adaptive logic. The target marker and far-threshold markers show where the controller is trying to stay and when far-mode recovery can engage.

resample shows the current adaptive correction around neutral 1.0. Left means slower, right means faster. The panel also exposes the active band/state so you can see whether the system is near, far, or actively recovering.
autoTune.openButtonTitle: Run the PI auto-tuner on the local resampling controller
autoTune.title: PI Auto-tune
autoTune.intro: Auto-tune the local resampler PI controller.
autoTune.prep: Play a long, stable audio source before starting. The tuning lasts roughly 12-15 minutes and modifies kp / ki / max_adjust / update_interval_callbacks in live. Initial values are restored on Cancel.
autoTune.persistReminder: Values are applied live but NOT persisted. Click the main Save button after Accept to write them to config.yaml.
autoTune.holdHint: Doubling Kp every 30 s until oscillation is detected on rate_adjust_ppm.
autoTune.kiBestKept: Ki iteration cap reached; using best value seen.
autoTune.perturbationPrompt: Pause your audio source for 2-3 seconds, then resume it. When done, click Continue.
autoTune.longRunHint: Watching the system over ~10 minutes to size max_adjust.
autoTune.tighteningHint: Verifying the system stays stable for 30 s…
autoTune.errorNoOsc: No oscillation reached at Kp={kp}. System may be heavily damped or source unstable.
autoTune.refusedNotEnabled: Adaptive resampling is disabled. Enable it before running the auto-tuner.
autoTune.refusedPaused: The resampling controller is paused. Resume it before running the auto-tuner.
autoTune.sourceLostHint: Audio source went unstable. Restart your source then click Resume.

master.title: Master
distance.title: Distance Diffuse
autoGain.title: Auto-gain (anti-clip)
help.master.gain: Master output gain applied to the whole mix, in dB (the slider is a linear ×0–2 factor; 0 dB = unity). The gauge beside the title shows the post-master output level with a peak-hold marker.
help.master.autoGain: Auto-gain (anti-clip): automatically pulls the master gain down when the output would clip, then eases it back up — a safety net rather than a mix tool. The dot lights up on clipping.
help.master.ceiling: The maximum output level (dBFS) auto-gain keeps the signal under. Lower leaves more headroom (safer); higher is louder but closer to clipping.
distance.modelInfoBody:
Distance model controls how object gain falls with distance before any diffuse or spread-specific processing is applied.

None keeps distance neutral. Linear and quadratic apply progressively stronger attenuation. Inverse-square is the steepest and is closest to a simple physical falloff.
hybrid.title: Hybrid backend
hybrid.curveHint: Blend curve — X: distance (center → cube surface), Y: external ratio. Double-click to add a point, double-click a point to remove it.
help.hybrid.selectedPoint: The blend-curve point currently picked on the graph above. Enter its exact distance (d: 0 at the centre, 1 at the cube surface) and external-backend ratio (0–1) here for precise placement instead of dragging.
barycenter.title: Barycenter backend
barycenter.infoBody:
Barycenter backend places energy by blending nearby speakers around a weighted center instead of using the VBAP triplet selection logic.

Localize increases how tightly energy collapses toward the target point. Lower values stay broader and softer; higher values bias toward a more focused image.
spread.title: Spread
experimentalDistance.title: Distance backend
experimentalDistance.infoBody:
Distance backend is an experimental renderer that scores speakers from their geometric relationship to the target point.

The exposed controls tune how many speakers can participate, how aggressively nearest speakers dominate, and how much position error is tolerated before gains are clamped or spread wider.

Use it for backend comparison and tuning, not as the safest default.

status.bridgeErrorTitle: Decoder bridge not found — spatial audio disabled
status.foreignRendererTitle: Connected to a renderer this Studio did not start
vbap.status.noAck: engine did not answer — is it the renderer you expected?
help.speaker.layout: Reorder this speaker within the layout (Up / Down) or remove it. The order defines the channel index.
help.speaker.position: Speaker position around the listener (listener at the origin). The Cartesian and Polar views always stay in sync on screen — editing one recomputes the other. The radio button picks which one is authoritative: that representation is the form stored in the layout and the one sent to the renderer when you move the speaker, so its values are kept exact instead of being re-derived through a conversion (which can drift on round-trips). Pick Cartesian to pin exact X/Y/Z, or Polar to pin exact azimuth/elevation/distance — the rendering pipeline itself always works in Cartesian. The “Real (m)” row mirrors the same position in metres, derived from the room dimensions, and “3D Edit” lets you drag the speaker directly in the scene.
help.speaker.positionMeters: The same cartesian position expressed in real-world metres (X left/right, Y rear/front, Z down/up), derived from the room dimensions. Editing a metre value moves the speaker and updates the normalised values above; both views stay in sync.
help.speaker.gain: Per-speaker output gain, in dB (the slider is a linear ×0–2 factor).
help.speaker.delayMs: Per-speaker output delay, in milliseconds. Kept in sync with the sample delay below.
help.speaker.delaySamples: Per-speaker output delay, in samples at the output rate. Kept in sync with the millisecond delay above.
help.speaker.delayTools: “Calc delays” derives every speaker's delay from its distance; “Delay → Dist” does the inverse, setting distance from the current delay.
confirm.calcDelays:
Calculate delays from distances?

This overwrites the delay of EVERY speaker so they are time-aligned to the farthest speaker (nearer speakers get more delay). Existing per-speaker delays will be replaced.
confirm.delayToDist:
Convert delays to distances?

This MOVES every speaker along its current direction so its distance matches its delay (the farthest speaker is the reference). Speaker positions will be overwritten.
confirm.resetVirtualBed:
Reset the fixed-channel source placement to defaults?

Every channel is moved to its default position in cartesian mode. Your current per-channel positions will be overwritten.
help.speaker.spatialize: Whether this speaker takes part in object panning. Off makes it a fixed bed / LFE channel that is not used as a VBAP vertex.
help.speaker.freqLow: Low edge of this speaker's crossover band, in Hz. Empty = full range; below this the speaker receives nothing.
help.speaker.freqHigh: High edge of this speaker's crossover band, in Hz. Empty = full range; above this the speaker receives nothing.
mpvOverlay.title: mpv overlay
outputMode.mpvNote: mpv host: the output mode is applied at player start — restart playback after switching.
backendParamHelp.sharpness: Cosine-lobe exponent: higher = tighter localisation, lower = more spread.
backendParamHelp.localize: Higher values collapse energy more tightly toward the target point; lower values stay broader and softer. Barycenter blends nearby speakers around a weighted center instead of VBAP triplet selection.
backendParamHelp.spread_min: Lower bound of the spread range. A point source (no size, no distance spread) pans at this value.
backendParamHelp.spread_max: Upper bound of the spread range, reached by a full-size object or, with distance spread, at the listener.
backendParamHelp.spread_from_distance: Derive spread from the object's distance instead of its size: closer objects spread wider. This is a pure function of position, so it is baked into the precomputed table.
backendParamHelp.spread_distance_range: Normalised distance at which distance-based spread falls back to zero.
backendParamHelp.spread_distance_curve: Curve exponent applied to the distance-based spread ramp.
backendParamHelp.size_to_spread_mode: How a 3-D object-size triplet (w, d, h) is reduced to a scalar spread. Object-size spread is applied live and is honoured only in realtime evaluation.
